summary: Wave equation for a string of length L with fixed ends. Press Play on the graph to watch it move; the motion repeats every 1.

methods.name: Separation of variables
methods.reason: With both ends fixed, the motion is a sum of standing waves.

steps.title: Separate the variables
steps.text: Look for solutions that are a product of a function of each variable. Substituting and dividing by the product puts each variable on its own side, so both sides equal a constant, written \(-\lambda\).

steps.title: Solve the eigenvalue problem
steps.text: The boundary conditions apply to the spatial factor. Only \(\lambda > 0\) gives non-zero solutions, and they are sines.

steps.title: Solve the time equation
steps.text: Each mode oscillates in time at its own frequency \(\omega_n = c\,n\pi/L\). All of them repeat after the period \(2L/c = 1\).
latex: T'' + c^2\lambda_n T = 0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad T_n = a_n\cos\omega_n t + b_n\sin\omega_n t

steps.title: Superpose
steps.text: Any sum of these standing waves satisfies the equation and keeps both ends fixed.

steps.title: Match the initial displacement
steps.text: At \(t = 0\) the series must equal \(f(x)\). The coefficients are the expansion coefficients of the data in the eigenfunctions, found with their orthogonality.

steps.title: Match the initial velocity
steps.text: The string starts at rest, so every \(b_n\) is zero.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Checked numerically: the series satisfies the equation at sample points and the boundary conditions. With 20 terms it reproduces the initial displacement closely.

methods.verify_note: Checked numerically: the series satisfies the equation at sample points and the boundary conditions. With 20 terms it reproduces the initial displacement closely.

methods.name: d'Alembert's formula
methods.reason: On a string the solution is always two travelling waves, so it can be written without a series.

steps.title: Write the general solution as two travelling waves
steps.text: Every solution of the wave equation is a wave moving right plus a wave moving left, each with speed \(c\).

steps.title: Fit the initial data
steps.text: Matching the initial displacement \(f\) and velocity \(g\) gives d'Alembert's formula. To respect the fixed ends, \(F\) and \(G\) are \(f\) and \(g\) extended as odd functions with period \(2L\): the waves then reflect upside down at each end.

steps.title: Use that the string starts at rest
steps.text: With \(g = 0\) the integral vanishes: the initial shape splits into two half-height copies travelling in opposite directions.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Agrees with the series solution at sample points, and it reproduces the initial data exactly.

methods.verify_note: Agrees with the series solution at sample points, and it reproduces the initial data exactly.
